n: This revelation came over two days in Kirtland as Joseph Smith and six elders, recently returned from missions, prayed together in unity. Joseph later called it a revelation on priesthood.
The Lord’s purpose for his latter-day Church: to restore scattered Israel, as the prophets foretold, and gather the Saints to Mount Zion—the New Jerusalem.
The city is to begin at a temple site in Independence, Missouri, which Joseph Smith and others had dedicated in August 1831 under the Lord’s direction.

f.g: A site in Independence, Jackson County, Missouri, dedicated August 3, 1831.

n: The New Jerusalem will be built as the Saints gather, starting at the temple site. The Lord says the temple will be raised “in this generation.”

f.g: Built, raised up.

n: A house of the Lord will be built, and his glory will rest on it as a cloud—like the cloud that filled the ancient tabernacle and Solomon’s temple. The Saints were later driven from Jackson County, and the Lord addressed that delay in D&C 124:49-51.

f.w: a cloud shall rest upon it

n: The revelation now traces the priesthood back in time, starting with the “sons of Moses”—those who hold the priesthood Moses received from his father-in-law, Jethro.

f.g: A priest of Midian and Moses’s father-in-law.

n: Jethro received the priesthood from Caleb—not the Caleb of Joshua’s day, but an earlier person known only from this revelation.

f.g: Known only from this list; not the same as Caleb son of Jephunneh in Numbers.

n: Caleb received it from Elihu. These names show a real, unbroken chain of authority passed by the laying on of hands.

f.g: An ancient priesthood holder known from this revelation.

n: Elihu received it from Jeremy, another figure otherwise unknown in scripture.

f.g: An English form of the name Jeremiah; this man is not the prophet Jeremiah.

n: Jeremy received the priesthood from Gad—again someone known only from this line, not the son of Jacob or the prophet Gad of David’s time.
Gad received it from Esaias, the next link back toward Abraham.

f.g: Greek form of Isaiah; this Esaias lived in Abraham’s time and is not the prophet Isaiah.

n: Esaias received the priesthood directly from God—a reminder that all true priesthood authority begins with him.
Esaias was a contemporary of Abraham and received a blessing from him, linking this line to the great patriarch.
Abraham received the priesthood from Melchizedek, the righteous king of Salem, whose own authority came down through his ancestors back to Noah.
From Noah the line goes back to Enoch through their family line.
And from Enoch back to Abel, who was murdered by Cain’s plot. Abel received the priesthood from his father Adam, the first man, at God’s command.

f.w: Adam, who was the first man

n: This higher priesthood continues in God’s true church in every age. It is “without beginning of days or end of years” because it is eternal, like God himself.

f.w: without beginning of days or end of years
f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation of Hebrews 7:3 clarifies that this phrase describes the priesthood, not Melchizedek himself.

n: The Lord also gave a priesthood to Aaron and his descendants—the Aaronic or lesser priesthood. It too continues alongside the higher priesthood “after the holiest order of God.”
The higher (Melchizedek) priesthood administers the full gospel and holds the key to knowing God—the deepest truths of his kingdom.

f.w: the key of the knowledge of God

f.g: Sacred truths known only by revelation.

n: Through its ordinances—like baptism, confirmation, and temple covenants—God’s power to make people godly is shown and given.

f.g: The divine power that makes people more like God.

n: Without those ordinances and proper authority, that power isn’t made manifest to mortal people. This is one reason the Restoration of priesthood mattered so much.

f.g: In mortal life.

n: Without this power, no one can see God the Father and live. Priesthood ordinances prepare people to enter God’s presence.
Moses taught this clearly to Israel in the wilderness and worked hard to make his people holy so they could see God.
But Israel hardened their hearts and could not bear God’s presence, so he swore they would not enter his “rest” in the wilderness—the fulness of his glory.
So God removed Moses and the higher priesthood from among the people as a whole.

f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation of Exodus 34:1-2 adds that the second set of tablets omitted the higher priesthood ordinances.

n: The lesser priesthood remained. It holds the key of the ministering of angels and the “preparatory gospel”—the first steps that prepare people for more.

f.g: The basic gospel of faith, repentance, and baptism that prepares for greater light.

n: That preparatory gospel—repentance, baptism, forgiveness, and the law of Moses—stayed with Aaron’s line until John the Baptist, who was filled with the Holy Ghost even before birth.

f.g: The outward rules of the law of Moses, focused on physical observances.

f.w: filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb

n: John was baptized as a child and, when eight days old, was ordained by an angel to prepare the way for Christ, overthrowing the corrupt religious power of his day.

f.w: make straight the way of the Lord
in whose hand is given all power

n: Elders and bishops are offices that grow out of, and belong to, the higher priesthood.

f.g: Parts attached to a larger whole; offices that branch from the priesthood.

n: Teachers and deacons are offices belonging to the lesser (Aaronic) priesthood, first given to Aaron and his sons.
Returning to the “sons of Moses”: priesthood holders of both orders will offer an acceptable offering in the Lord’s house to be built on the consecrated site.
These priesthood holders will be filled with God’s glory in his house on Mount Zion. The Lord tells the elders that they are these “sons of Moses and of Aaron.”
Those who faithfully receive both priesthoods and “magnify” their callings are made holy by the Spirit, even to the renewing of their bodies.

f.g: Making a calling great by serving with full effort and faith.

n: They become heirs of Moses, Aaron, and Abraham—God’s covenant people and chosen ones.
Here begins the “oath and covenant of the priesthood”: those who receive the priesthood receive Christ himself.
Receiving the Lord’s servants means receiving the Lord who sent them.

f.w: he that receiveth my servants receiveth me

n: And receiving Christ means receiving the Father who sent him.
Receiving the Father brings his kingdom—indeed “all that my Father hath.” It is the greatest promise God can make: to share everything he has.
This is what the oath and covenant of the priesthood means. God promises with an oath; the person covenants to be faithful.
Everyone who receives the priesthood receives this covenant from the Father, and he will never break it or move away from it.
But someone who receives it and then breaks it by turning completely away will not be forgiven, in this world or the next—a very serious warning about total, willful apostasy.

f.g: Completely abandons it—not merely stumbling, but fully and knowingly turning away.

n: Sorrow awaits those who refuse this priesthood. The Lord personally confirms it on the men present and assigns angels to watch over them.
A new section begins: be careful of yourselves and pay close attention to the words that lead to eternal life.
We are to live by every word that comes from God—quoting what Jesus told Satan in the wilderness.

f.w: every word that proceedeth forth from the mouth of God

n: A chain of truths: God’s word is truth, truth is light, and light is Spirit—the Spirit of Jesus Christ.
This Spirit, often called the Light of Christ, gives light to every person born. Those who listen to it receive more light.

f.w: giveth light to every man that cometh into the world

n: Listening to the Spirit leads a person to God the Father.
The Father teaches such people about the covenant he has renewed with the Saints—given not only for them but for the blessing of the whole world.

f.w: for the sake of the whole world

n: Without that covenant, the world lies in sin, groaning in darkness and bondage.

f.g: Moans in distress.

n: The sign of this bondage is that people do not come to Christ.
Anyone who does not come unto Christ remains captive to sin. Christ alone frees us.
Those who reject Christ’s voice don’t truly know it and aren’t his. His sheep know his voice.
This is how to tell the righteous from the wicked—and why the world groans under sin even now.
The Lord turns to the Church: their minds had been darkened by unbelief and by treating sacred things too casually.

f.g: Took casually; did not value as sacred.

n: That vanity and unbelief had put the whole Church under condemnation.

f.g: Emptiness, pride, or worthless pursuits.

n: This condemnation rests on all the children of Zion, without exception.

It will remain until they repent and remember the “new covenant,” the Book of Mormon, and the earlier commandments—not just talking about them but living them. Church leaders have repeatedly applied this to how members value the Book of Mormon.

f.w: the new covenant, even the Book of Mormon
not only to say, but to do

n: They must produce fruit worthy of the Father’s kingdom, or else judgment will come on Zion’s people.

f.g: Fruit that is fitting or worthy.

n: The Lord will not let his people pollute the holy land he has promised them.
To those who heard these words directly, he promises blessing if they receive them.
Their sins are forgiven on condition that they stay serious and prayerful and bear testimony to the world of what has been revealed to them.

f.g: Seriousness and reverence of mind.

n: They must take the gospel into all the world, and where they can’t go personally, they must send others.

f.w: go ye into all the world

n: Christ calls these elders his apostles, God’s high priests, gifts from the Father—and his friends.

f.w: whom my Father hath given me

n: As with his ancient apostles, anyone who believes their words and is baptized for the remission of sins will receive the Holy Ghost.

f.w: baptized by water for the remission of sins

n: Miraculous signs will follow those who believe—an echo of the Savior’s words at the end of Mark.

f.w: these signs shall follow them that believe

n: Believers will do many wonderful works in Christ’s name.
They will cast out evil spirits in his name.
They will heal the sick in his name.
They will heal blindness and deafness, as Jesus himself did.

f.w: open the eyes of the blind

n: Those unable to speak will speak.

f.g: Unable to speak (not a comment on intelligence).

n: Poison given to them will not hurt them.
Even snake venom will not harm them.
But they must not boast of these miracles or show them off to the world. Gifts of the Spirit are for blessing and saving people, not for display.

f.w: for your profit and for salvation

n: Those who reject the message and refuse baptism will be “damned”—stopped in their progress—and cannot enter the Father’s kingdom.

f.g: Condemned; stopped from progressing to God’s presence.

n: This command is in force from this moment for the whole world. The gospel is for everyone who has not yet received it.
Even those who have the kingdom must be called to repentance: some Saints for their unbelief, and members in Zion for rebelling against the elders when they visited earlier.

f.g: Scolded, rebuked.

n: From now on Christ calls them friends. He wants them to travel and preach in his power, as his disciples did when he was on earth.
Those early disciples went without money bags, food sacks, or extra coats, trusting God completely.

f.g: A money pouch or a traveling bag for food.

n: They are sent to test the world. And a worker deserves to be supported by those he serves.

f.g: Test.

f.w: the laborer is worthy of his hire

n: Faithful missionaries are promised strength of mind and body, and God will notice every detail of their lives—even a single hair. They will not go hungry or thirsty.

f.w: a hair of his head shall not fall to the ground unnoticed

n: So don’t worry about tomorrow—about food, drink, or clothing.

f.w: take ye no thought for the morrow
f.g: Don’t be anxious about tomorrow.

n: Look at the wildflowers: they don’t work or weave, yet they’re dressed more beautifully than any kingdom’s glory.

f.w: consider the lilies of the field
toil not, neither do they spin
f.g: Don’t labor or spin thread to make cloth.

n: Your Father in Heaven knows you need all these things.
So let tomorrow take care of itself.
Don’t prepare speeches ahead of time; instead, constantly store up the words of life in your mind, and you’ll be given what to say at the very moment it’s needed.

f.w: treasure up in your minds continually the words of life
it shall be given you in the very hour

n: This applies to everyone called to the ministry: from now on, go without purse or scrip when proclaiming the gospel.
Missionaries are sent to call the world to repent of its wrongdoing and to warn of a coming judgment.

f.g: Correct, rebuke.

n: A tender promise: Christ will go before them, be on their right and left, put his Spirit in their hearts, and surround them with angels to hold them up.

f.w: I will go before your face

n: Whoever welcomes them welcomes Christ, and will feed, clothe, and support them.
Those who help them will surely be rewarded.

f.w: shall in nowise lose his reward

n: Those who refuse to help are not true disciples; caring for the Lord’s servants is a mark of discipleship.

f.w: by this you may know my disciples

n: If someone rejects them, they should leave privately, wash their feet as a witness before God, and not return to that person. This is a solemn act, not a casual gesture.
They are to do the same in any village or city that rejects them.
Still, they must search diligently and not hold back. Sorrow comes to any home or town that rejects them and their testimony of Christ.

f.g: Don’t hold back; give full effort.

n: The warning is repeated for emphasis—rejecting Christ’s witnesses is serious.
The Almighty has laid his hand on the nations to discipline them for their wickedness.

f.g: Punish, as with a whip.

n: Plagues will continue until the Lord finishes his work, which he will cut short in righteousness for the sake of his elect.
In the end, everyone who remains will know the Lord, from least to greatest. They will see eye to eye and together sing a new song.

f.w: from the least unto the greatest

n: The new song begins: the Lord has restored Zion and redeemed Israel by his grace, fulfilling the faith and covenants of their ancestors.

f.g: Being chosen by God’s grace, not by our own merit.

n: Satan is bound, time as we know it ends, and all things are gathered in one in Christ. Zion comes down from heaven and rises up from the earth to meet it.
The earth, like a mother giving birth, brings forth its full strength. Truth springs up from it, heaven smiles upon it, and it is clothed in God’s glory because he dwells with his people.

f.g: Labored in childbirth.

f.w: truth is established in her bowels

n: The song ends in praise: glory, honor, power, and might belong to God, who is full of mercy, justice, grace, truth, and peace forever.
Practical instructions begin. Missionaries with families who receive money as gifts should send it home or use it for their families, as the Lord directs.
Those without families should send money they receive to the bishop in Zion or Ohio to fund printing the revelations and building Zion.

f.g: The revelations were being prepared for publication as the Book of Commandments.

n: If someone gives them a new coat or suit, they should give the old one to the poor and go on their way happily.
Those strong in the Spirit should take along someone weaker so that person can grow strong too, with humility on both sides.

f.g: Built up, strengthened spiritually.

n: Elders should take Aaronic Priesthood holders with them to set up meetings, prepare the way, and fill appointments the elders can’t reach.

f.g: Arrange preaching meetings.

n: This is how the ancient apostles built up the Church.
Each person should serve in his own role. Using Paul’s image, the body needs its feet as much as its head.

f.w: let not the head say unto the feet

n: Every member is needed so all can be built up together and the whole “system” stays healthy and complete.

f.w: the body hath need of every member

n: High priests, elders, and priests should travel and preach, while teachers and deacons serve as “standing ministers” to watch over local congregations.
Bishop Newel K. Whitney is to travel among the branches looking for the poor and caring for them, humbling the rich and proud in the process.

f.g: A Kirtland merchant called as bishop in December 1831.

n: He should hire an agent to handle his business affairs as he directs.

f.g: Worldly, everyday (as opposed to religious).

n: Bishop Whitney is also to warn New York City, Albany, and Boston that they face desolation if they reject the gospel. He and Joseph Smith traveled east that fall.
If those cities reject the message, their judgment is near and their house will be left empty—words Jesus spoke over Jerusalem.

f.w: their house shall be left unto them desolate

n: If he trusts the Lord he won’t be put to shame, and God will watch over him in every detail.

f.g: Put to shame, defeated.

n: The other elders should go as their circumstances allow to the major cities and towns, clearly explaining the “desolation of abomination” coming in the last days.
The Lord will tear down worldly kingdoms. Not only the earth but even the starry heavens will tremble.
Though they can’t see it yet, the Lord has already set heaven’s powers in motion. Soon they will see it and know he will come to reign with his people.
The revelation closes with Christ as Alpha and Omega—the one who frames all of history.
